title: From God to the Atom and Back
subtitle: A travelogue from the frontier of fundamental physics: "Looks like Ancient Greece"

blocks.html: When I was a little boy, likely in response to an aggravating series of questions, my father (a physician) explained that reality is basically made up of little bits of stuff--protons, neutrons, electrons, photons--and the fundamental forces that push them around. The forces bind subatomic particles into atoms, electromagnetism binds atoms into crystals and molecules, molecules into  Like most kids, my exposure to this ontology was lightweight until at least high school. I recall a few mentions in science class, conversations with my parents or brother, a book about black holes for young readers, and exhibition materials at the "earth and space" museum. My dad and the wider culture were introducing me to the long tradition of materialist reductionism, a lineage often identified with Democritus, from whom we get the word "atom."
